scope: Complete float64 numerical policy-gradient pipeline and bounded full-dimension synthetic training. No Gym/Atari environment, checkpoints, rendering or unbounded training.

two_layer_validation.source_mode: Hash-verified original definitions are executed in an isolated dictionary; model, gamma and episode inputs are supplied explicitly. No source imports, environment creation, top-level assignments, IO or infinite loop execute.
compatibility: Python2 syntax is converted before selecting the five definitions; xrange becomes range.
The removed np.float alias is changed to np.float64 by AST transformation; the NumPy module is not monkey-patched.
The bounded harness uses a local RandomState(23) instead of unspecified global random state. C# and Python retain the same initialization-then-action draw sequence.
Hidden width is reduced to8 for the short loops; full210x160x3 frames and6400 inputs are retained. The existing full H200/D6400 byte gate remains separate.
Synthetic observations and action-dependent point rewards replace Gym only. Original normalization, accumulation, batch10 and RMSProp equations remain unchanged.

short_run.interop: Each NumSharp RGB frame is exported zero-copy into the original Python preprocessing function; mutation is observed back through ndarray.item<byte>(). The trained W1 is imported into an owning NumSharp array.
short_run.assertions: Finite per-step policy/hidden states, complete episode progression, finite standardized returns/gradients, a real parameter update, cleared gradient buffers, positive RMS cache and readable reimported trained state.

byte_gate.purpose_of_extra_episode: Episode11 uses the weights updated at episode10 and checks fresh accumulation after the prior gradient buffer was cleared.
comparison_points: Initial W1/W2, gradient buffers and RMS caches
Every raw input snapshot, full mutated frame, preprocessed vector, difference vector, hidden state, probability, RNG draw, action, score derivative and point reward
Every stacked episode input/hidden/score/reward array, discounted return, normalized advantage, weighted score and both gradients
Every preupdate accumulated buffer and postepisode model, buffer, cache, reward total, running reward, episode count and update count
byte_gate.fallback: None: every numeric array comparison requires identical dtype, shape and canonical bytes.

recorded_result.scope: This is the successful byte-ledger test only. The separate short-run test in this initial artifact stopped on a test-side missing channel index; that read was corrected to row,column,0 with explicit RGB shape checks for the next central run.

original_numpy_probe.meaning: Measured with the reviewed original five definitions and the bounded harness before central C# test execution; invented point rewards are not Atari scores. Final C# test outcomes are reported by the central TRX artifacts.

python_first.method: Independent NumPy numerical expressions were executed before the C# implementation; no full source script or Gym loop was executed.
python_first.interpretation: These are explicitly chosen numerical fixtures, not measurements reported by the original unseeded training script.

assertions: All five original numerical functions execute through a complete10-episode/40-frame run with a real RMSProp update.
NumSharp.Interop.pythonnet exports frames zero-copy; original mutation is observed in NumSharp and trained weights are imported back into NumSharp.
limits: Synthetic environment, hidden8 and local seed23 are explicit bounded-test adaptations; no Atari capability or original unbounded training result is claimed.

assertions: Every intermediate and persistent numeric state matches the original NumPy functions throughout11episodes/44frames, including the default10-episode update and a subsequent episode using updated weights.
Strict dtype/shape/byte comparisons, zero ULP budget, no tolerance fallback; original loader hash and selected-definition inventory asserted.
limits: Short loop uses hidden8 while retaining6400 inputs; original H200 is covered independently by Full200By6400_SeededInitializationForwardAndBackward_Exact.
Original functions are unchanged numerically; a bounded driver supplies observations/rewards and reproduces top-level normalization/batching/update equations without Gym/IO.

assertions: All1280000 W1 and200 W2 coefficients match NumPy at original H200/D6400, using source sqrt-dimension scaling.
The next uniform draw also matches, proving initialization and action sampling share the same RNG stream.
limits: Seed3 is an explicit reproducibility fixture; the source does not supply a fixed seed.

assertions: 210x160x3 uint8 input; rows35:195, stride2, red channel, background144/109 erased and other nonzero pixels binarized.
All6400 output values and all100800 bytes of the mutated source frame are checked; unsampled pixels/channels remain unchanged; returned float64 data owns its storage.
limits: Original np.float alias is spelled float64 for current NumPy.
The original slice assignments mutate selected frame pixels; this side effect is intentionally preserved, not hidden.

assertions: First observation produces an all-zero motion vector; later input is current minus previous with identical float64 values.
limits: The bounded rollout resets its previous frame per episode, as the source does at line129.

assertions: Sigmoid agrees exactly for finite inputs and saturated infinite/large-magnitude inputs.
Action2 is chosen only when uniform draw is strictly below probability; equal draw selects action3; log-policy derivative is selected-label minus probability.
limits: Action-selection/log-gradient source lines80:87 supplement sigmoid lines27:28.
Invalid probabilities/draws/actions fail explicitly instead of silently propagating invalid policy state.

assertions: Every probability and every4x200 hidden state agrees with live NumPy over the same inputs/weights.
Per-frame matrix-vector dot is retained; it is not replaced by a potentially differently rounded batch matrix-matrix product.
limits: Exact floating dot bytes require matching BLAS build, threads and CPU dispatch; tests use the interop suite's pinned backend.

assertions: Backward recurrence resets before incorporating each nonzero point reward.
Both vector and actual stacked (T,1) shapes are tested; empty discount output and gamma validation are explicit.
limits: Float64 returns are the numerical contract.

assertions: First subtract mean, then compute standard deviation of the already-centered values, matching the source's sequential in-place normalization.
Means and squared-residual reductions use the NumPy-compatible explicit-axis pairwise path; raw result bytes match.
limits: Zero/nonfinite standard deviation is rejected rather than letting the original divide-by-zero produce NaN advantages and corrupt the model. This is an explicit robustness adaptation, not original error parity.

assertions: The weighted action-score signal, ReLU derivative mask, full200x6400 W1 gradient and200-element W2 gradient match actual NumPy.
Source lines111:113 advantage weighting and gradient accumulation are included in full episode state checks.
All15 parameters of a3-hidden/4-input reduced model are checked against central differences of the advantage-weighted log-policy objective.
Step1e-6, absolute gradient error bound5e-8; chosen preactivations stay away from ReLU's nondifferentiable zero.
limits: Finite differences validate calculus, not byte parity. This reduced independent check supplements, and does not replace, full original-dimension byte tests.

assertions: Inputs/hidden states/log gradients/rewards have consistent time-major shapes.
The original default10-episode batch leaves weights unchanged for9 episodes and updates on10; buffer reset is asserted.
A separately configured two-episode batch compares all model weights, gradient buffers and RMS caches after each episode against NumPy.
limits: The two-episode live case is an explicit smaller batch configuration, not a claim that the original default was2.

assertions: Learning rate1e-4, decay0.99, cache=decay*cache+(1-decay)*gradient², ascent update divided by sqrt(cache)+1e-5.
Two successive updates assert every weight/cache element and zeroed gradient bytes.
limits: The port updates stable cache/buffer objects in place rather than replacing Python dictionary entries; numerical state is identical.

assertions: Episode/update counters, episode reward total and initial/subsequent exponentially smoothed running reward are asserted.
limits: Reward totals in these tests are supplied data, not measured Atari scores.

assertions: Weights snapshot input arrays; long-lived model and optimizer state survive caller NDScope disposal.
Trainer owns its buffers/cache and borrows the separately disposable model.
Incompatible network/episode/optimizer shapes, unsupported dtype and invalid batching/discount/optimizer parameters are rejected.
limits: Additional validation is a documented port API contract, not a claim of matching Python exception classes or all malformed-input behaviors.

assertions: The full H200/D6400 model processes moving-pixel210x160 frames, samples actions, constructs advantages/gradients and completes2 episodes with1 real parameter update.
The parameter-change norm is finite and positive; final probability and running-reward bounds are asserted.
limits: Observations and point rewards are deliberately fabricated; this is not Atari/Pong-v0, learned Pong ability, convergence, a benchmark or a reproduced score.
The original unbounded interaction loop is never executed. Demo batch2/steps6/seed0 are presentation defaults; the asserted reduced rollout uses explicitly stated seed7.

exclusions.reason: Pong-v0 creation/reset/step and Atari assets/ROMs are not reproduced. Policy inputs/rewards are supplied by the caller or by the explicitly synthetic demonstration.

The source runs forever and supplies no fixed seed, rollout recording, learned-score target, episode budget or timing claim. Passing numerical tests is not evidence of learning Pong or a runtime benchmark.
Python cPickle load/save and hundred-episode checkpoint scheduling are not ported; no checkpoint is downloaded, loaded or fabricated.
Environment rendering, Python2 print syntax and celebratory punctuation are presentation effects, not part of the numerical parity claim. Their reward/counter inputs are tested.
